terms.comment: A member of the Roman senate, and of the councils of other peoples, the Nervii or the Rhodians (Lewis & Short). Traupman gives it for a modern senator, man or woman; Morgan–Owens for a member of any deliberative body, a town councillor included. Lewis & Short find senātrix, a woman senator, only in Priscian.

phrases.latin: mōs anteā senātōribus Rōmae fuit in cūriam cum praetextātīs fīliīs introīre
phrases.english: it used to be the custom at Rome for senators to bring their young sons with them into the senate house

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. legislator, member of parliament; city councilman.
